key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that retrieval-augmented generation can teach theoretical computer science effectively by grounding LLM answers in curated proofs, slides, and worked examples.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests a practical blueprint for AI tutoring systems in math-heavy CS courses, combining domain-aware retrieval with pedagogically ranked explanations.
method: Built a domain-specific RAG system on textbooks, 847 slides, 312 solved problems, 156 proof templates, and 89 worksheets.
Added mathematical entity recognition, notation-aware retrieval, and pedagogical re-ranking to improve answer quality.
Evaluated on 179 curated exam-style questions across complexity theory and algorithms topics.
evidence_signal: On 179 questions, AlgoRAG achieved 100% success with 38.0 s mean response time, ROUGE-1 F1 of 0.0963, ROUGE-L F1 of 0.0683, and pedagogical quality of 0.7620.
watch_item: BLEU-4 was zero, so the system’s quality depends on reasoning and pedagogy metrics rather than surface n-gram overlap, which can undercount valid mathematical explanations.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
